title: orchestrate-credential-fabric-and-async-generator-bridge
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: Multiple SDK teams requested a small, consistent surface for credential fallback and streaming ergonomics. Customers reported integration friction when migrating long-lived streaming consumers (chat/observable pipelines) between Python/TS/Go — token refresh timing, retry floor semantics, and typed async generator shapes diverged. This PR introduces the "credential fabric" concept: a lightweight orchestration layer that centralizes credential selection/fallback, prefetch 'stitch' mode, and a small compatibility shim that yields a unified async-generator/iterator surface across languages. Motivation: reduce app-side glue, enable shared retry presets, and make typed stream consumers portable across SDKs without breaking existing integrations. Summary of changes: - Introduces a credential-fabric layer in the monorepo that exports a language-agnostic contract for: preferred credential, fallback queue, prefetch/stitch hints, and heartbeat-aware TTLs. - Python SDK: add redwood.cred_fabric.CredentialOrchestrator (async) + typed AsyncGenerator helpers (py SDK v2.5.0). Improves __aiter__/aclose behavior so cancelation races are deterministic. - TypeScript SDK: add async-generator facade with typed envelope and a small pullstream helper that understands the fabric prefetch hints; bump TS SDK to v1.29.0. - Go SDK: introduce IteratorWithCtx type and a credential adapter that exposes the fabric's lease and heartbeat; go-sdk bumped to v1.9.0. - Retry semantics: introduce an adaptive-retry-floor preset (stabilizes retry backoff when credential switch occurs to avoid thundering reconnections). - Backcompat: provide a thin compatibility shim for legacy consumers (v1.x) that continue to use older iterator shapes; new default surface is opt-in via SDK config flag enable_cred_fabric. - Tests: cross-sdk integration tests that run a simulated token-rotation storm and validate latency/incident metrics. Migration notes: - To opt into the new unified stream surface, set SDK config enable_cred_fabric=true. - For Python users: replace manual token-refresh loops with CredentialOrchestrator.subscribe() AsyncGenerator. - For TS/Go: adapters mirror the Python flow; examples added under redwood/examples/streaming/cred-fabric. Performance and telemetry: On representative streaming workload (50k short streams), end-to-end median connect latency reduced by ~8% and recovered error-rate under token rotation improved 3x due to the adaptive-retry-floor. Rollout plan: feature flag gated, staged rollout to beta customers, SDK docs + migration guide included. CI/QA: unit tests added for all three SDKs, cross-sdk e2e run in matrix. See release_notes for user-facing summary.

release_notes:
- Introduce Credential Fabric: centralized credential selection and prefetch hints across SDKs
- Python: CredentialOrchestrator async API (py v2.5.0) and deterministic cancelation
- TypeScript: typed async-generator facade and pullstream adapter (ts v1.29.0)
- Go: context-friendly iterator and cred adapter (go v1.9.0)
- Adaptive retry floor preset to reduce reconnection storms during token rotation
- Opt-in via enable_cred_fabric flag; migration guide added in docs/sdk-migration/credential-fabric.md
